newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents per lb higher on Friday, as traders expected the market to bounce back after Thursday's steep losses.

New York arabica futures tumbled on Thursday, battered by speculative and trade selling. July slid 21.05 cents per lb, to 230.50 cents, after ranging between 252.00 and 228.00 cents. Second-month September fell 15.70 cents, to 209.40 cents, while the back months closed 6.25 to 9.90 lower.
The July/September spread continued to shrink from more than 40 cents seen last week, closing at to 21.10 cents today from 26.45 cents on Wednesday.
Some traders said July options expiry today could weigh on the market, as traders try to push the market down toward the 220.00 strike price.
Technically, traders said July would find resistance at 240.00, while support was seen at 225.00.
After Thursday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 427 60-kg bags as of June 4, to 45,275 bags, There were 2,885 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Weather Services Corp. said on Friday no damaging cold weather was expected to hit Brazil's coffee belt on Sunday and Monday, although temperatures will drop to below normal levels.
In London, robusta futures were down sharply at midday Friday, but off earlier lows. LIFFE July dropped $70 at the break, to $1,835, after bottoming at $1,815. September was $75 lower, at $1,855.
